description: The graph illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of various methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and IKE—across different co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^0$ to $10^4$ and the y-axis showing ACC (%) from 40% to 65%. The Base method (black line with circle markers) shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 39% to 44% as the co-occurrence number increases. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) starts at around 44% and rises to about 56%, showing a consistent upward trend. The FT method (blue line with triangle markers) begins at roughly 40% and increases to approximately 48%. The MEMIT method (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at about 43% and climbs to around 55%. The IKE method (red line with triangle markers) begins at approximately 43% and increases to about 49%. The green line with square markers, which appears to represent a baseline or combined method, starts at around 51% and rises to about 66%, indicating the highest performance across all co-occurrence numbers. All methods exhibit an increasing trend in accuracy with higher co-occurrence numbers, with the green line consistently outperforming the others.
